rows.title: As CT patches one hole in social safety net, are others developing?
rows.standfirst: CT legislators said they will study whether most services are shrinking even as programs for people with developmental disabilities expand.

rows.title: Winter heating assistance in CT projected to plummet
rows.standfirst: Connecticut families on emergency heating assistance could get nearly $1,000 less in government aid this winter without more state support.

rows.title: How does CT tax retirement earnings? Here’s what to know
rows.standfirst: A new CT tax cut package expanded existing exemptions and other tax breaks for retiring income, involving pensions, annuities and IRAs.

rows.title: Is CT’s sales tax holiday real relief — or just a gimmick?
rows.standfirst: Sales tax holidays are too limited to provide any meaningful tax reform, according to a new analysis from a progressive policy group.

rows.title: Auditors: UConn overpaid Herbst $355k during sabbatical
rows.standfirst: Auditors found that two employees were granted a year of sabbatical leave while collecting their full salary, in violation of UConn’s bylaws.

rows.title: Do taxes make people leave CT? Policy group says not so much
rows.standfirst: High housing costs and low investments in education, transportation and other core services could make CT less attractive than high taxes do.

rows.title: CT may not be done cutting income taxes yet
rows.standfirst: Advocates seeking an ongoing child tax credit have fallen shy of their goal over the past two years but say their support base has grown.

rows.title: Senate leader supports 5-year phase-in for CT child tax credit
rows.standfirst: A CT child tax credit has a better chance of becoming real now that CT’s highest-ranking state senator offered an alternate route this week.
